requirement: Describe VIVID as a prospective randomized controlled study in Black outpatients with three parallel arms: Black-participant video, White-participant video, and usual-care clinician counseling.

evidence.text: randomized ... to 1 of 3 arms ... video with black participants ... video with white participants ... usual care

notes: Do not describe the behavioral intervention as a device trial merely because ICD implantation is an outcome.

requirement: State 1:1:1 allocation across the three randomized arms.
notes: The protocol does not provide a block size or stratification rule; do not invent one.

requirement: Limit the masking claim to participants being blinded to differences between the two videos; do not call the whole three-arm study double-blind.
acceptable_values: participants blinded to differences between video versions only

evidence.text: Study participants will be blinded to differences in the 2 videos.

notes: Usual care versus video cannot be concealed from participants in the same sense.

requirement: Report the protocol target of approximately 480 participants, 160 per arm, and do not silently replace it with the later SAP's 309-analyzable-subject calculation.

evidence.text: Approximately 480 patients ... 160 black video, 160 white video, 160 UC

notes: The hidden reference SAP documents an enrollment-driven update. In protocol_only this is not a fact the model can infer.

requirement: Define the sole primary outcome as the decision to accept ICD implantation at 7 days after baseline.

evidence.text: The primary outcome will be the decision for ICD implantation at 7 days.

notes: Racial concordance was changed from co-primary to secondary before the final protocol/SAP pair.

requirement: Use the primary contrast of both video arms combined versus usual care.
acceptable_values: Black video plus White video versus usual care

evidence.text: combined video groups ... compared between ... video intervention ... and usual care

notes: A three-arm omnibus test is not the prespecified primary contrast.

requirement: Analyze the primary proportions with Pearson's chi-square test, falling back to Fisher's exact test if counts are small.

evidence.text: compared with the Pearson chi-square test ... if necessary, the Fisher Exact Test

notes: Equivalent notation such as chi-squared is acceptable.

requirement: Report each primary proportion, the between-group difference in proportions, and its 95% confidence interval in addition to the p-value.

evidence.text: provide estimates of proportions with their confidence intervals

notes: The protocol's estimand scale is a difference in proportions, not only an odds ratio.

requirement: Use two-sided alpha 0.05 for the final single primary comparison.

evidence.text: All quantitative tests will be two-sided and conducted at the 5% level

notes: The earlier two-co-primary design used 0.025 per comparison; it is historical, not the final rule.

requirement: State that racial concordance is secondary and that secondary comparisons receive no type-I-error adjustment; report all prespecified comparisons.

evidence.text: changed from a co-primary outcome to a secondary outcome ... no adjustment for type I error

notes: Do not retain the obsolete Bonferroni co-primary structure as the final plan.

requirement: Cover the key secondary outcomes without promoting them to primary: racial concordance in ICD acceptance, knowledge change, decisional-conflict change, ICD implantation by 90 days, and patient-provider time.

evidence.text: Other outcomes include ... racial concordance ... knowledge ... decisional conflict ... ICD receipt within 90 days

notes: Qualitative interviews are a separate mixed-method component and need not be forced into the quantitative SAP core.

requirement: Keep the two post-intervention anchors distinct: ICD decision and questionnaires at 1 week, and ICD implantation status at 90 days.
notes: Seven days and one week are equivalent here.

requirement: Do not invent an ITT, modified-ITT, or complete-case population definition; ask which randomized participants enter the primary analysis and how unavailable 7-day decisions are handled.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering randomized set and missing day-7 outcome

evidence.text: The protocol specifies the comparison but not an operational primary analysis population.

notes: The reference SAP also does not provide a sufficiently operational population rule.

requirement: Ask how a missing or indeterminate 7-day ICD decision is treated; do not silently code missing as no, unsure, failure, or exclusion.

evidence.text: Follow-up and the primary comparison are described without a missing-outcome rule.

notes: This missing decision materially changes the denominator and risk difference.

requirement: Ask whether the primary analysis should adjust for site or use site-robust uncertainty; do not invent a center effect when the protocol only states recruitment from up to 15 sites.

evidence.text: Approximately 480 patients will be enrolled from up to 15 active sites.

notes: A simple chi-square test is explicit, but the multicenter handling is not.
